title: Bird Flu Kills Washington Dairy Worker in First Death Linked to Infected Cattle

content:
The World Health Organization said on Tuesday, Nov. 24, that the United States has reported three confirmed human cases of bird flu in Washington state, including one death — the first death anywhere in the world linked to exposure to infected dairy cattle.

All three patients were adults who worked on dairy farms in Yakima County, Washington, where the H5N1 avian influenza virus was recently detected in cattle. Genetic sequencing confirmed all three infections were caused by H5N1, with strains closely matching the virus circulating in the state’s dairy herds.

The first patient developed symptoms on Oct. 5, including eye irritation, a runny nose, muscle aches and headache, and sought care on Oct. 12. That patient was not hospitalized and was offered treatment with the antiviral oseltamivir.

The second patient had underlying medical conditions, developed severe respiratory illness, was hospitalized and died on Nov. 1. The third patient developed conjunctivitis and recovered without hospitalization.

The WHO said there is no evidence so far of human-to-human transmission. As of Nov. 20, a total of 75 human cases of H5N1 infection had been reported in the United States since 2024. Washington confirmed its first infected dairy herds on Oct. 8, and the outbreak has since spread to 33 herds in Yakima County and a dairy in Benton County. Oregon has also confirmed its first infected dairy herd, becoming the 22nd state with the virus in cattle.

Health officials say the risk to the general public remains low, but the Yakima death is a reminder that the virus can cause severe illness, particularly in people with underlying health conditions. Webb County is ranching country, and local ranchers are already on alert after two screwworm cases were confirmed here this month. Officials urge anyone working with livestock to watch animals for signs of illness and call a veterinarian immediately if an animal appears sick.

Sources: World Health Organization, Nov. 24, 2026; Reuters, Nov. 24, 2026; Yakima Health District; Associated Press.
